name: TX-03
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent Keith Self's cash and outside-spending advantage
No public polls or expert ratings; Hunt has only $44k on hand
model.rationale: The seat's eleven-point Republican lean, Self's incumbency and financial edge, and markets pricing his win chance near 94% all point the same way, and no polling or expert ratings indicate a competitive race.
model.watch: Fresh polling showing Hunt within single digits or a wave of Democratic outside spending would be the first sign of a genuine contest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 3rd District, in the Dallas suburbs, leans strongly Republican, and incumbent Keith Self is running for reelection after securing renomination. Democrat Evan Hunt has raised a modest sum but enters the fall with limited cash on hand, while Self holds an edge in both direct fundraising and outside support. No public general-election polling is available, and no major expert ratings list the race as competitive.

Prediction markets give Self roughly a 94% chance of holding the seat, consistent with the district's eleven-point Republican lean. The open question is whether the national political environment can narrow the margin; even a strong Democratic year would require an unusually large swing to put this seat in play. On the current evidence, Self is clearly favored, with Hunt needing nearly everything to break his way to contend.
